title: Capital Budgeting — NPV, Profitability Index, and Payback
scenario: Meridian Building Group is evaluating a $800,000 investment in prefabrication equipment expected to generate after-tax net cash inflows of $230,000 at the end of each of the next 5 years, with no salvage value. Meridian's after-tax weighted-average cost of capital is 12%. Use the present-value factor in the exhibit; round dollar answers to the nearest dollar and ratios/years to two decimals.

exhibits.label: Exhibit A — Project data and 12% factor

tasks.prompt: Requirement 1 — Compute the present value of the inflows and the project's net present value.
tasks.explanation: PV of inflows = $230,000 × 3.604776 = $829,099. NPV = $829,099 − $800,000 = $29,099. NPV is positive, so the project earns more than the 12% cost of capital and adds value.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 2 — Compute the profitability index and the (undiscounted) payback period in years.
tasks.explanation: Profitability index = PV of inflows ÷ initial investment = $829,099 ÷ $800,000 = 1.04 (> 1.0, consistent with the positive NPV). Payback = $800,000 ÷ $230,000 = 3.48 years, which ignores the time value of money and every cash flow after payback.
